#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Downloads frame_001.png .. frame_028.png one by one, slowly and carefully.
# Uses absolute paths only, so it works no matter where you run it from.

set -u
set -o pipefail

BASE_URL="https://flappingairplanes.com/airplane-smooth-frames"
DEST_DIR="/home/kushal/src/ts/kphoto/public/images/flapping-airplanes"
FIRST=1
LAST=28
DELAY_SECONDS=5

if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: curl is not installed. Install it with: sudo dnf install curl" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR" || {
    echo "ERROR: could not create $DEST_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Checks the file starts with the 8-byte PNG signature
is_valid_png() {
    local sig
    sig="$(head -c 8 "$1" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"
    [ "$sig" = "89504e470d0a1a0a" ]
}

failed=()
total=$((LAST - FIRST + 1))
count=0

for i in $(seq "$FIRST" "$LAST"); do
    count=$((count + 1))
    name="$(printf 'frame_%03d.png' "$i")"
    url="${BASE_URL}/${name}"
    dest="${DEST_DIR}/${name}"
    tmp="${dest}.part"

    echo "[$count/$total] $name"

    # Skip files that are already downloaded and valid
    if [ -f "$dest" ] && is_valid_png "$dest"; then
        echo "    already exists and is a valid PNG, skipping"
        continue
    fi

    rm -f "$tmp"

    if curl --fail --location --silent --show-error \
            --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 --retry-all-errors \
            --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 120 \
            --user-agent "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Fedora; Linux x86_64)" \
            --output "$tmp" \
            "$url"; then
        if is_valid_png "$tmp"; then
            mv -f "$tmp" "$dest"
            size="$(stat -c %s "$dest")"
            echo "    saved ($size bytes)"
        else
            echo "    ERROR: downloaded file is not a valid PNG" >&2
            rm -f "$tmp"
            failed+=("$name")
        fi
    else
        echo "    ERROR: download failed for $url" >&2
        rm -f "$tmp"
        failed+=("$name")
    fi

    # Be polite to the server
    if [ "$i" -lt "$LAST" ]; then
        sleep "$DELAY_SECONDS"
    fi
done

echo
if [ "${#failed[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Done. All $total frames are in: $DEST_DIR"
else
    echo "Finished with ${#failed[@]} failure(s):" >&2
    printf '  %s\n' "${failed[@]}" >&2
    echo "Re-run the script to retry only the missing ones." >&2
    exit 1
fi

Our mission is to unlock new markets in AI, including robotics, scientific discovery, and more, by improving unit economics for whole industries. We believe the only way to do this is to co-evolve models and systems, bridging the traditional divides between software and hardware. These wins compound multiplicatively; the history of AI supports this theory.</p><p class="description">Systems work makes GPUs more efficient—cheaper inference &amp; training—but can also make GPUs more expressive. We have developed the world’s most complete megakernel framework. It allows us to use weird architectures, weird optimizers, and to overlap memory-bound inference with compute-bound training inside the same kernel. It can already perform entire training runs, serve inference, play video games, and even do all three simultaneously in a single kernel. But we’ve barely scratched the surface of GPUs, and we think they’re more flexible and valuable than most believe.</p><p class="description">In recent months, the majority of our work has built on top of these new primitives. What I found
How the original animates: it’s a flipbook, not physics. The site loads airplane-smooth-frames/frame_000…028.png as WebGL textures and picks one each frame with frame = floor(time × 12) % 29. React and regl handle the rendering, and a fluid simulation runs around the plane.
Scroll effect: as you scroll, the plane tilts up to 14° over the first 60% of a screen, then fades out between 48% and 66% using a smoothstep curve.
Frames: you have frame_001–frame_028, but the original also has frame_000. That’s fine, since 28 frames still loop correctly. Each frame is 900×723 black ink on cream paper.
Repo: dump.txt matches the right repo at commit 2cb6447, and the baseline passed 452 unit tests and typechecked cleanly before my changes.
Built so far (not delivered yet)
The new page: /labs/flapping-airplane/ (and /es/…), plus a /labs/ index and a “Labs” link in the header.
<kp-flipbook> component: Play/Pause, step forward/back, a frame scrubber, a frames-per-second slider (1–60) and a “Climb” slider using the original tilt and fade curves. It also shows a live readout of t, t × fps, the frame index and the file name, plus a filmstrip of all 28 frames.
Three switchable drawing techniques: swapping an <img> source, drawing into a <canvas>, and pure CSS @keyframes with step-end. The CSS version plays even with JavaScript off.
Polite defaults: frames are preloaded and decoded before playback starts. The flipbook starts paused if your system asks for reduced motion, and stops its loop when scrolled off-screen. Speed, drawing technique and play/pause are remembered in kphoto:flipbook:v1.
The page text: eight short sections explaining each technique, with code samples.
